title: Buster Smith and One O'Clock Jump
summary: Albert calls Buster Smith the greatest, mentions Frank Driggs's session, and claims Smith wrote One O'Clock Jump; the block ends in a garbled ASR loop.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: How was Buster Smith in those days? Buster's the greatest. He's still the greatest.
He plays now, but he has lost most of his teeth and he's playing on the organ, but he's also

playing. Besides, the other day, Frank Drake's called me and wanted me to come up to New York and do a session and he wanted me to get hold of Buster's number. But I don't know what happened to that thing, Dick. But he wanted to get Buster's number. And I gave him Buster's number. But I don't know what happened to that thing, Dick. I never was called to go to this session. And I was helping him. And I talked to John Hardy. You remember John Hardy? Yeah. And he said, I don't know what happened to that thing. I don't know what happened to that thing. I never was called to go to this session. But he wanted to get Buster Smith and all the old-timers. And I was helping him to talk to John Hardy. Yeah, he was in my band. But he's a teacher and he's reluctant to leave and go anywhere. reluctant to leave and go anywhere. So I don't know, maybe still in Macon, I'm going to talk to Frank when I get back to San Antonio.
What did Buster Smith sound like then? What did he sound like?
Well, I've heard him on records, but you know, I... Gee whiz, he was a tremendous arranger.

But he's one of the first clarinetists that would play like, oh, Buster Biel and Noah and fellas like that. And there was a clarinetist, I'm trying to think of his name, in Dallas. He left and went to Europe.

When you once told me there was a Buster Biel in Texas, it was not the same guy that was with Henderson. No, it was different. That may be the same name. I just wondered if he used strange harmonies or Buster Smith, you know, they compare him with Charlie Parker and all that.

Well, not that type of playing, no, but he was a fantastic musician as far as tonation and knowing his instrument because he could also do good arranging. He was responsible for Con Basie's theme song, One O'Clock Jump. He wrote that and Basie went ahead and like the other people done, just went ahead and said, it's his number, but it's actually Buster Smith song. I didn't know. That's right. Well, I see in those days, Con Basie was around there with the Blue Devils.
